title: Prevent sexual acquisition of HIV with twice-yearly injections

concept.text: Provide effective HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis with six-monthly maintenance injections. Lenacapavir achieved this dosing interval, with HIV testing and management of resistance risk remaining essential. Proposed completion test: FDA approval for PrEP in HIV-negative adults and adolescents weighing at least 35 kg, supported by phase 3 HIV-incidence endpoints and a maintenance injection interval of six months. Test set by: FDA; PURPOSE trial protocols supplied the incidence comparisons accepted in the approval. Reported achieved: FDA approved lenacapavir (Yeztugo) for PrEP on 18 June 2025. Sources given: [FDA original Yeztugo prescribing information](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/220020s000lbl.pdf) ; [Current Yeztugo label and approval record](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=1c241af1-ce62-4b0a-9eb7-f6b626174f01).

page.title: Twice-yearly injectable HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis
page.definition: An antiretroviral regimen reduces sexual acquisition of HIV-1 in people without HIV, with maintenance injections every six months. Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) means taking medicine before potential exposure to prevent infection.

goal.need: An estimated 1.3 million people acquired HIV worldwide in 2024. CDC reports that approximately half of US users of daily oral PrEP discontinue it within 6–12 months. Twice-yearly PrEP offers an alternative to daily medication.

statements.quote: LEN’s twice-yearly dosing offers a significant advantage for people who face challenges with adhering to daily oral PrEP
the CDC PrEP Guidelines Work Group strongly recommends lenacapavir injections as an HIV PrEP option

completion.title: FDA approves HIV-1 pre-exposure prophylaxis given by injection every six months.
completion.criterion: FDA approves a medicine for pre-exposure prophylaxis to reduce the risk of sexually acquired HIV-1 in adults and adolescents weighing at least 35 kg, with maintenance doses injected no more often than every 26 weeks. The label reports randomized, double-blind, active-controlled phase 3 trials in which HIV-1 incidence on the regimen was lower than both the estimated background incidence and the incidence on daily oral emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate: one trial in cisgender women (2,134 assigned the regimen in the first such label) and one in cisgender men, transgender women, transgender men and gender non-binary people (2,179). Dosing more often than every 26 weeks does not count.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration: Yeztugo (lenacapavir) approval letter for NDA 220020, 18 June 2025, and prescribing information, sections 1, 2.3 and 14.
completion.threshold_quote: YEZTUGO is indicated for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) to reduce the risk of sexually acquired HIV-1 in adults and adolescents weighing at least 35 kg who are at risk for HIV-1 acquisition.
completion.basis: A first: before 18 June 2025 FDA had approved no HIV prevention medicine dosed twice a year. The approval fixes the indication, population and schedule: after initiation doses on days 1 and 2, 927 mg is injected subcutaneously every 26 weeks (±2 weeks), with an HIV-1 test before each injection. The trial populations, sizes and comparisons are those of section 14 of the label. The statistical tests FDA agreed for the two trials are milestones m4 and m5; no further efficacy threshold is added here.

milestones.title: Nonclinical studies support reasonably safe initial human testing of a long-acting HIV capsid inhibitor.
milestones.criterion: Animal or in vitro pharmacology and toxicology justify the sponsor’s conclusion that the proposed initial human investigation is reasonably safe. The 2020 lenacapavir paper reports a mean half-maximal effective concentration of 105 pM against HIV-1 in eight independent cell-culture experiments, each with four biological replicates, and refers to supporting nonclinical safety studies.
milestones.set_by: FDA, 21 CFR 312.23(a)(8), the pharmacology and toxicology requirement for an investigational new drug application.
milestones.threshold_quote: it is reasonably safe to conduct the proposed clinical investigations.

milestones.title: Lenacapavir enters a phase 1 study of safety and pharmacokinetics in humans.
milestones.criterion: Introduce the investigational drug into humans in a closely monitored phase 1 study assessing pharmacological actions, exposure and adverse effects. Study GS-US-200-4070 enrolled 40 HIV-negative adults: 32 received lenacapavir and eight placebo. Its 2020 report found that the 300 mg and 450 mg groups, eight participants each, maintained plasma concentrations above 3.87 ng/mL for more than 24 weeks. That concentration is a protein-adjusted laboratory 95% effective concentration, not a validated human prevention threshold.
milestones.threshold_quote: Phase 1 includes the initial introduction of an investigational new drug into humans.

milestones.title: A long-acting capsid inhibitor reduces experimental infection risk in macaques at P < 0.05.
milestones.criterion: Reduce acquisition of SHIV, a simian–human immunodeficiency virus used as a model, versus control under the published study’s Cox regression analysis, with two-sided P < 0.05. The study published on 7 December 2021 included 24 rhesus macaques, eight per group. GS-CA1, a lenacapavir analogue, reduced per-exposure infection risk by 97% in the 300 mg/kg group (P = 0.0001); five of eight animals remained uninfected through 24 weeks.
milestones.set_by: The GS-CA1 study investigators, including Gilead Sciences and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, in the published macaque-study methods. This test concerns a lenacapavir analogue.
milestones.threshold_quote: Comparisons were considered statistically significant at a two-sided alpha level of 0.05

milestones.title: Twice-yearly lenacapavir meets FDA’s phase 3 test against estimated background HIV incidence.
milestones.criterion: At each planned interim analysis, the lenacapavir/background HIV-incidence ratio must have a point estimate <0.5 and a 95% confidence-limit upper bound <0.8, with one-sided α = 0.0026. Background incidence estimates acquisition without PrEP. PURPOSE 1, in cisgender women, recorded zero infections among 2,134 lenacapavir recipients; PURPOSE 2, in men and gender-diverse persons, recorded two among 2,179. Ratios versus background were 0.00 (95% CI 0.00–0.04) and 0.04 (0.01–0.18), respectively. Both passed.
milestones.set_by: FDA Division of Antivirals, agreed PURPOSE 1 and PURPOSE 2 interim-analysis success criteria reproduced in section 8 of its Breakthrough Therapy Designation review.
milestones.threshold_quote: (bHIV) < 0.8 with the point estimate being < 0.5 (1-sided alpha of 0.0026).

milestones.title: Twice-yearly lenacapavir prevents HIV better than daily emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate.
milestones.criterion: After passing the background-incidence test, demonstrate superiority to daily oral emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate using incidence-rate ratios and one-sided α = 0.0026. The interim analysis occurs when 50% of randomized participants have completed at least 52 weeks or discontinued. PURPOSE 1’s oral comparator had 16 infections among 1,068 participants; the lenacapavir/comparator ratio was 0.000 (95% CI 0.000–0.101; P < 0.0001). PURPOSE 2’s comparator had nine among 1,086; its ratio was 0.111 (0.024–0.513; P = 0.00245). Both passed.
milestones.set_by: FDA Division of Antivirals, agreed key secondary interim-analysis criteria; the sequential tests and results appear in section 14 of the original Yeztugo prescribing information.
milestones.threshold_quote: followed by YEZTUGO compared to TRUVADA, all at alpha level of 0.0026

results.finding: GS-6207 showed a mean HIV-1 EC50 of 105 pM in eight independent cell-culture experiments, each with four biological replicates.
results.detail: The paper reports minimal cytotoxicity in human cells and refers to supporting nonclinical safety studies, supporting initial human testing.

results.finding: In 40 HIV-negative adults (32 active, eight placebo), GS-6207 maintained concentrations above the laboratory paEC95 for >24 weeks in both higher-dose groups.
results.detail: The randomized, double-blind phase 1 study assessed safety and pharmacokinetics. The 300 mg and 450 mg groups each included eight recipients. The 3.87 ng/mL benchmark is a protein-adjusted laboratory EC95, not a validated human prevention threshold.

results.finding: GS-CA1 reduced SHIV acquisition versus vehicle in 24 rhesus macaques (eight per group), with P = 0.0001 for the high-dose group.
results.detail: The 300 mg/kg group had a 97% per-exposure risk reduction; five of eight remained uninfected through 24 weeks. Cox proportional hazard regression accounted for changing challenge dose and used a two-sided significance threshold.

results.finding: PURPOSE 2: lenacapavir recipients (n=2,179) had an HIV incidence-rate ratio of 0.04 versus estimated background incidence.
results.detail: The 95% CI was 0.01–0.18, meeting the point-estimate <0.5 and upper-bound <0.8 requirements. The planned interim analysis used one-sided α=0.0026; P<0.001. This source reports PURPOSE 2 results.

results.finding: PURPOSE 2: lenacapavir (n=2,179) versus daily F/TDF (n=1,086) yielded an HIV incidence-rate ratio of 0.11.
results.detail: The 95% CI was 0.02–0.51; P=0.002 passed one-sided α=0.0026 after the background-incidence test. The planned interim trigger was 52-week follow-up or withdrawal for 50% of target enrollment. There were two versus nine infections.

results.finding: Lenacapavir showed a median EC50 of 40 pM against eight subtype B HIV-1 isolates.
results.detail: The label reports cell-culture activity and animal toxicology, but does not establish the sponsor’s conclusion that the proposed initial human investigation was reasonably safe.

results.detail: The indication covers adults and adolescents weighing at least 35 kg. The supplied excerpt identifies both randomized, double-blind, active-controlled trials but ends before their comparative efficacy results.
